dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: the dependency list is exactly framework + adapter, and every hand-rolled bit replaces a library rather than duplicating one.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.js — all API access, caching and naming helpers live in one module; pages never fetch directly — an Astro upgrade or data-shape change touches one file
app/astro.config.mjs:1-6 — six-line config, nothing exotic or internal-reliant

app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:36-44 — hand-rolled escapeHtml + chainToHtml building HTML strings injected via set:html (:228); duplicating the compiler's escaping job is a churn and injection risk

app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:17-24, abilities/[name].astro:17-24, types/[name].astro:26-33, pokemon/[name].astro:16-21 — identical try/catch-404 boilerplate copy-pasted in four pages; Astro 7.4's notFound() handler / advanced routing would centralize it
app/src/lib/pokeapi.js — untyped plain-JS data layer; no JSDoc/TS types at the API boundary despite typed Props on components
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and config are well centralized so framework or API moves ripple little, but the manual HTML-string rendering, per-page 404 boilerplate and untyped boundary add avoidable maintenance surface.

findings.issue: Evolution chain is built as concatenated HTML strings with a hand-rolled escapeHtml, injected via set:html — manual escaping that must be kept correct by hand and bypasses the framework's escaping.
findings.suggestion: Render the tree with a small recursive Astro component (or a slot-rendered nested list) so the compiler handles escaping, or at minimum centralize escapeHtml in the data layer module.

findings.issue: The try/catch-fetch → 404-status → NotFound-render block is duplicated verbatim in all four dynamic routes (also abilities/[name].astro:17-24, types/[name].astro:26-33, pokemon/[name].astro:16-21).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared loader (e.g. fetchOrNotFound in lib/pokeapi.js) or move to Astro 7's advanced-routing entrypoint with the new notFound() handler to define the behavior once.

findings.issue: Client scripts use is:inline, skipping Vite processing (no bundling, deduping or TypeScript); the second copy sits in pokemon/[name].astro:299.
findings.suggestion: Consider Astro's default processed <script> (or a shared module) so the scripts are bundled, type-checkable and deduped as the code grows.

findings.issue: popstate handler falls back to location.reload(), discarding the partial-refresh logic it already has for filter changes.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the same refresh(url) + DOMParser path on popstate so back/forward behaves like filter changes without a full reload.

findings.issue: The data layer is untyped plain JS; the shape of API responses (species, pokemon, move records) is implicit, so changes to the PokeAPI shape would surface as runtime errors rather than at the boundary.
findings.suggestion: Add JSDoc typedefs or convert the module to .ts so the API boundary is typed like the components' Props already are.

summary: This app is on the bleeding edge: astro 7.4.4 and @astrojs/node 11.1.9 are literally today's latest stable releases, the SSR setup matches current docs, and no deprecated Astro 7 APIs appear anywhere. It is platform-first with exactly two dependencies and a single well-defined data module, so most upgrades would touch very little. The deductions are hand-rolled HTML string assembly with manual escaping, copy-pasted 404 boilerplate across four routes, and an untyped data boundary — all easy, contained fixes.

apis.replacement: Astro's default processed <script> is the more idiomatic choice for bundleable, TS-capable client code
